args.summary: The latest production deploy of checkout-api, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in production. Per the runbook, a rollback was executed to v2.3.0 — the most recent release that was healthy in production. The rollback rolled out successfully to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with status "rolled_out". Health of the service should be verified post-rollback; the v2.3.1 deployment needs investigation (note: its staging predecessor v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy, suggesting the issue may have been detectable before promotion).
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Checked release history** for checkout-api. Found that the latest production deploy, **v2.3.1**, was unhealthy, while **v2.3.0** was the most recent version that had been healthy in production.

2. **Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0** across all production regions. The rollout completed with status `rolled_out` in us-east, us-west, and eu-west.

3. **Opened incident INC-0001 (SEV2)**, titled "checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0". The incident pages the on-call engineer and documents the rollback and current state, including a note that the staging precursor `v2.3.1-rc` was also unhealthy — a useful clue for whoever investigates the root cause of v2.3.1's failure.

4. **Verified post-rollback health**: checkout-api is now running v2.3.0 in all regions, reporting `healthy: true` with a low error rate (~0.2%).

No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 was a previously healthy production release.
